description: # CS2106 Lecture 1 Overview. ## Uploaded by. AI-enhanced title and description. This document provides an introduction and overview of a lecture on operating systems. It includes information about the instructor, office hours, required textbook, workload expectations, assessment breakdown, important dates, and the lecture format. The philosophy of "lighting a fire, not filling a bucket" is introduced. An overview of topics to be covered is given, including complex systems, abstraction and interfaces, concurrency, resource management, and performance trade-offs. title: CS2106 Introduction to Operating Systems
description: # CS2106 Introduction to Operating Systems. **Module**: CS2106 Introduction to Operating Systems. This module introduces students on the concepts of the operating system and is taken after CS2100 Computer Organisation. It also covers other concepts on operating system protection mechanisms, as well as operating system structures and architectures. As it was the first semester where lectures are entirely online due to COVID-19, it was a little messy at the start as people were getting used to it, but eventually Dr Cristina found ways to keep us engaged, such as allowing annotations before the lecture starts to get some feedback from students. The tutor will start with a recap of the week's concepts, followed by going through some of the tutorial questions, before ending with a multiple choice quiz where you need to get a certain number of questions right before you can get the 1% credit for that week. There were a total of 5 lab assignments, where each assignment would span 2 weeks and will test a particular concept taught in class (mainly related to interacting with the operating system).
